rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Validate and normalize real-world structured-data fields directly in SQL -- email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, EU VAT numbers, credit-card numbers, URLs, and postal codes.

This worker turns the data-cleaning steps you would normally script in Python into set-based DuckDB functions: check whether a value is well-formed, rewrite it into a canonical form for joining/deduplication, or pull out a part (a domain, a country, a brand). Reach for it whenever a table holds messy contact, banking, or payment fields that must be filtered, standardized, or bucketed before use.

Two ideas run through the whole surface. First, every operation is offline and deterministic -- validation checks syntax, structure, and checksums (mod-97 for IBAN, Luhn for cards, per-country rules for VAT and postal codes) but never performs a DNS or network lookup, so it is safe over huge tables. Second, outcomes are total and predictable: NULL input yields NULL output; an invalid non-NULL value yields false from a validity test and NULL from a formatter or extractor -- nothing raises (the one deliberate exception is an unknown postal-code country, which errors so a typo is not mistaken for an invalid code).

Phone and VAT operations accept an optional ISO region/country argument (US and the EU-prefixed form are the defaults); postal-code validation requires an explicit country.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# conform: Field Validation & Normalization in SQL

**Validate and normalize phone numbers, emails, IBANs, EU VAT numbers, credit-card numbers, URLs, and postal codes directly in DuckDB SQL** -- no UDF plumbing, no external service, and no network calls. The `conform` extension turns the data-cleaning steps you would normally script in Python into fast, set-based SQL functions, so you can check validity, standardize formatting, and extract field parts right where your data lives.

This catalog is built for anyone wrangling messy real-world contact, banking, and payment data: data engineers cleaning a CRM export, analysts deduplicating customer records, or pipelines that must reject malformed input before it lands. Every check is **offline, deterministic, and total** -- functions never raise on garbage (with one deliberate exception, an unknown postal-code country), returning `false` for `is_valid_*` and `NULL` for formatters and extractors. That makes the extension hermetic and safe to run over huge tables without DNS lookups or flaky I/O.

Under the hood, `conform` composes three best-in-class, battle-tested libraries. Phone parsing, validation, and E.164/national/international formatting come from [`phonenumbers`](https://github.com/daviddrysdale/python-phonenumbers) (the Python port of Google's [libphonenumber](https://github.com/google/libphonenumber)). IBAN, EU VAT, and the Luhn credit-card check come from [`python-stdnum`](https://github.com/arthurdejong/python-stdnum) ([documentation](https://arthurdejong.org/python-stdnum/)). Email syntax validation and normalization come from [`email-validator`](https://github.com/JoshData/python-email-validator). URL and postal-code handling are implemented in-process against per-country rules.

## What you get

The surface divides into three shapes -- **validity tests** that return a boolean, **normalizers/formatters** that rewrite a value into a canonical string (ideal for joining or deduplication), and **part extractors** that pull a single component (a domain, country, brand, or host) out of a well-formed value -- plus discovery tables that enumerate the phone regions and card brands the worker recognizes.

Phone and VAT functions take an optional ISO region/country argument (`'US'` and the EU-prefixed form are defaults); postal-code validation requires a country.

```sql
SELECT conform.main.normalize_email('Test@Example.COM');
SELECT conform.main.format_phone_e164('07911 123456', 'GB');
SELECT conform.main.mask_card('4111-1111-1111-1111');
```
